flawed_step: Step 1: The implication from 3-connectivity and claw-freeness to Hamiltonicity cannot be justified.
counterexample: Take the Petersen graph and replace each vertex by a triangle, assigning its three incident edges to the three distinct triangle vertices. The resulting graph is 3-connected and claw-free but non-Hamiltonian.
assessment_summary: Each vertex in the expanded graph has two adjacent neighbors within its triangle, so no induced claw exists. Deleting at most two vertices preserves connectivity because the Petersen graph is 3-edge-connected. Any Hamiltonian cycle would cross each replacement triangle in exactly two external edges; contracting all triangles would therefore produce a Hamiltonian cycle in the Petersen graph, which is impossible.
